prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

A welding or cutting device includes an internal combustion engine coupled to a generator for generating electrical power. A welding or cutting power supply is powered by the generator. The welding or cutting power supply supplies a welding or cutting output signal. An auxiliary outlet circuit is configured to receive power from the generator. The auxiliary outlet circuit includes at least one auxiliary load outlet. A controller controls an engine speed of the internal combustion engine. The controller is configured to determine an anticipated load on the generator to be supplied through the auxiliary load outlet, based on a no load condition of the auxiliary load outlet, and adjust an idle speed of the engine based on the anticipated load. The controller is further configured to subsequently increase the engine speed, from the idle speed to an auxiliary load speed, when the generator supplies power through the auxiliary load outlet.

outputs.L2:
A welding or cutting apparatus has an internal combustion engine connected to a generator that produces electric power. The generator energizes a welding or cutting power source, which provides a welding or cutting output signal. The system also includes an auxiliary outlet circuit arranged to take power from the generator and having at least one auxiliary load outlet.

A controller regulates the speed of the internal combustion engine. The controller is set up to identify an expected generator load that would be delivered through the auxiliary load outlet, using a no-load state of that outlet as the basis for the determination, and to modify the engine’s idle speed according to the expected load. After that, when the generator delivers power through the auxiliary load outlet, the controller raises the engine speed from the idle speed to an auxiliary-load operating speed.
outputs.L3:
The device includes an internal combustion engine that is mechanically coupled to a generator. During operation, the engine drives the generator, causing the generator to produce electrical power for use by the device.

A welding or cutting power supply is connected to receive electrical power from the generator. The power supply converts or conditions the generator power as needed and provides an output signal suitable for a welding or cutting operation. This allows the device to function as a self-contained welding or cutting system without requiring an external electrical supply.

The device also includes an auxiliary outlet circuit that receives electrical power from the generator. The auxiliary outlet circuit includes at least one auxiliary load outlet, which may be used to power external electrical tools, equipment, or other auxiliary loads.

A controller is provided to manage operation of the engine and generator. The controller determines an anticipated generator load associated with the auxiliary outlet based on a no-load condition of the auxiliary outlet circuit. Using this anticipated load information, the controller adjusts the engine idle speed. This adjustment allows the engine to idle at a speed selected to better accommodate expected auxiliary power demand while reducing unnecessary fuel consumption, noise, and engine wear when full output is not required.

After the idle speed has been set, the controller monitors operation of the generator and the auxiliary outlet circuit. When the generator begins supplying power through the auxiliary load outlet, the controller increases the engine speed from the adjusted idle speed to an auxiliary load speed. At this higher speed, the engine drives the generator with sufficient capacity to support the auxiliary load being supplied through the outlet.
outputs.L4:
A welding or cutting device is provided with an engine-driven power generation system capable of supplying electrical power for multiple purposes. The device includes an internal combustion engine coupled to a generator, which produces electrical output used to operate a welding or cutting power supply as well as an auxiliary power outlet. The auxiliary outlet may be used to power external tools, lights, chargers, compressors, or other electrical equipment at a work site.

A controller monitors and manages operation of the engine and generator so that sufficient power is available when needed. In particular, the controller is configured to regulate engine speed according to expected or detected auxiliary load conditions. Rather than waiting until a large auxiliary load is fully applied before increasing engine speed, the controller may anticipate the need for additional power and adjust the engine idle speed in advance. This preparatory increase allows the system to respond more quickly when a user connects or activates equipment through the auxiliary outlet.

When electrical power is actually supplied to the auxiliary outlet, the controller raises the engine from the adjusted idle speed to an auxiliary load speed appropriate for supporting the connected load. By doing so, the system maintains stable power output, reduces the likelihood of voltage drop or engine bogging, and improves overall performance during simultaneous or alternating welding, cutting, and auxiliary power use.

This control approach provides improved responsiveness compared with systems that remain at a low idle speed until after an auxiliary load is detected. It also helps optimize fuel consumption, noise, and engine wear by allowing the engine to operate at lower speeds when demand is low while still preparing the system for anticipated increases in load. As a result, the welding or cutting device can deliver reliable welding or cutting power and dependable auxiliary power in a more efficient and controlled manner.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest and most common words in the English language, yet it plays an important role in communication. It is called the definite article, and it helps point to something specific. When we say “a book,” we mean any book. But when we say “the book,” we mean a particular book that the listener or reader can identify.

This simple word gives clarity and focus. It helps us understand whether someone is talking about something general or something already known. For example, “the sun,” “the world,” and “the answer” all suggest something definite and recognizable.

Although “the” may seem ordinary, it is essential in everyday speech and writing. Without it, many sentences would sound incomplete or unclear. In a way, “the” shows that even the smallest words can have great importance.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for an engine-driven welding or cutting machine with a generator, auxiliary outlet, and controller that adjusts idle speed based on anticipated auxiliary load.
counterfactuals.output: An engine-driven welding or cutting machine includes an engine, a generator driven by the engine and configured to supply welding or cutting output power, an auxiliary power outlet coupled to the generator, and a controller operatively coupled to the engine. The controller is configured to operate the engine at an idle speed during a low-load condition and to determine an anticipated auxiliary load associated with the auxiliary power outlet before or during application of the auxiliary load. In response to the anticipated auxiliary load, the controller adjusts the idle speed to an elevated idle speed sufficient to support the auxiliary load while maintaining a desired generator output characteristic, such as voltage or frequency. The anticipated auxiliary load may be determined based on a sensed connection, a user selection, historical load information, a tool identification signal, or a detected pre-load condition. The controller may reduce the engine speed after removal or reduction of the auxiliary load to improve fuel efficiency and reduce noise while maintaining availability of auxiliary and welding or cutting power.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a concise invention summary describing a welding/cutting device powered by an internal combustion engine and generator, where the controller predicts auxiliary outlet load and changes engine speed accordingly.
counterfactuals.output: An engine-driven welding/cutting device includes an internal combustion engine, a generator driven by the engine, a welding/cutting output circuit, one or more auxiliary power outlets, and a controller. The controller monitors operating parameters associated with the auxiliary outlet, such as outlet current, voltage, power demand, or load transients, and predicts an impending auxiliary load requirement. Based on the predicted auxiliary load, the controller adjusts the engine speed before or as the load is applied, thereby increasing available generator output and reducing voltage sag, frequency deviation, or weld/cut performance degradation. The controller may lower engine speed during low-load conditions to reduce fuel consumption, noise, and emissions, and may raise engine speed when a predicted auxiliary load exceeds a threshold or indicates a rapid demand increase.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.output: A welder/generator system comprising: an engine; a generator driven by the engine and configured to generate electrical power; a welding power supply coupled to the generator and configured to provide a welding output to a welding output terminal; an auxiliary load outlet circuit coupled to the generator and configured to provide auxiliary electrical power to an auxiliary receptacle; and an engine speed controller operatively coupled to the engine, the welding power supply, and the auxiliary load outlet circuit, wherein the engine speed controller is configured to operate the engine at a reduced no-load speed when neither a welding load nor an auxiliary load is detected, and to increase engine speed to a loaded operating speed in response to detection of at least one of a welding load at the welding output terminal or an auxiliary load at the auxiliary receptacle, the engine speed controller further being configured to maintain or adjust the engine speed based on a magnitude or presence of the detected load to support delivery of welding power and auxiliary power.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an engine-driven welding or cutting power supply that manages idle speed by determining an anticipated generator load through an auxiliary outlet before increasing to an auxiliary load speed.
counterfactuals.output:
An engine-driven welding or cutting power supply can include an internal combustion engine coupled to a generator that provides power for welding/cutting outputs and for an auxiliary power outlet. The system uses an engine controller to manage engine speed between an idle speed and a higher auxiliary-load speed.

In operation, while the engine is running at idle, the controller monitors the auxiliary outlet to detect whether a load is connected or about to be applied. Rather than immediately accelerating the engine whenever the auxiliary outlet is used, the controller determines an anticipated generator load associated with the auxiliary outlet. This may be done by sensing electrical characteristics such as outlet voltage, current, impedance, power draw, or a change indicating that an auxiliary device has been plugged in or switched on.

Based on the anticipated generator load, the controller decides whether the load is large enough to require an increase in engine speed. If the expected load exceeds a threshold, the controller commands the engine to transition from idle speed to an auxiliary load speed suitable for supplying the auxiliary power demand. If the anticipated load is below the threshold, the controller may keep the engine at idle or delay increasing speed, reducing unnecessary noise, fuel consumption, and emissions.

Thus, the power supply manages idle speed proactively by evaluating the expected auxiliary generator load through the auxiliary outlet before increasing engine speed to support auxiliary power output.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Create a technical patent abstract about a combustion-engine generator for welding/cutting that supplies auxiliary outlets and uses a controller to set idle speed based on expected auxiliary outlet demand.
counterfactuals.output: A combustion-engine driven welding/cutting generator includes an engine, a generator coupled to the engine, a welding/cutting output circuit, one or more auxiliary power outlets, and a controller. The generator supplies electrical power to the welding/cutting output circuit and to the auxiliary power outlets. The controller is configured to determine an expected auxiliary outlet demand associated with one or more loads connected to, or anticipated to be connected to, the auxiliary power outlets. Based at least in part on the expected auxiliary outlet demand, the controller selects an idle speed for the engine from a plurality of idle speeds or determines a target idle speed. The selected idle speed is higher when the expected auxiliary outlet demand is greater, thereby maintaining sufficient generator output capacity for auxiliary loads while reducing fuel consumption, acoustic noise, and engine wear when lower auxiliary demand is expected. The controller may determine the expected auxiliary outlet demand from outlet usage history, sensed outlet current or voltage, operator input, load identification, tool type, receptacle selection, or welding/cutting operating state. The controller may further transition the engine between the selected idle speed and a welding/cutting operating speed in response to detected welding or cutting activity.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
